q: All matter is made of ____.
e: All matter is made of atoms. The physics in this sentence is built around atoms.

q: Atoms are composed of smaller particles called electrons, protons and ____.
e: Atoms are composed of smaller particles called electrons, protons and neutrons. Neutrons names atoms are composed of smaller particles called electrons, protons and.

q: There is a central nucleus made up of protons and ____.
e: There is a central nucleus made up of protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Around this, electrons orbit at high speed in allowed ____.
e: Around this, electrons orbit at high speed in allowed orbits. The physics in this sentence is built around orbits.

q: Protons have a positive charge and electrons have an equal negative charge, while the neutrons are ____.
e: Protons have a positive charge and electrons have an equal negative charge, while the neutrons are neutral. The physics in this sentence is built around neutral.

q: An atom has the same number of electrons as protons, so its total charge is ____.
e: An atom has the same number of electrons as protons, so its total charge is zero. The physics in this sentence is built around zero.

q: Thus, atom as a whole is ____.
e: Thus, atom as a whole is neutral. The physics in this sentence is built around neutral.

q: Together, protons and neutrons are known as ____.
e: Together, protons and neutrons are known as nucleons. Nucleons names together, protons and neutrons.

q: Protons and neutrons have similar masses and electrons are the ____.
e: Protons and neutrons have similar masses and electrons are the lightest. The physics in this sentence is built around lightest.

q: Protons and neutrons are about 1800 times more massive than an electron, so all of an atom's mass is concentrated in its ____.
e: Protons and neutrons are about 1800 times more massive than an electron, so all of an atom's mass is concentrated in its nucleus. Nucleus here means the tiny positive core of an atom, protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: Electrons are held in orbit by the Coulomb attractive force of the ____.
e: Electrons are held in orbit by the Coulomb attractive force of the nucleus. Nucleus here means the tiny positive core of an atom, protons and neutrons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: Protons and neutrons are bound tightly together in the nucleus by the strong nuclear ____.
e: Protons and neutrons are bound tightly together in the nucleus by the strong nuclear force. Force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: The atomic number of an element tells us how many protons (or) electrons are in an atom of that ____.
e: The atomic number of an element tells us how many protons (or) electrons are in an atom of that element. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: It is written as symbol ____.
e: It is written as symbol $Z$. The physics in this sentence is built around $Z$.

q: Each element has its own unique atomic ____.
e: Each element has its own unique atomic number. The physics in this sentence is built around number.

q: The atomic number is sometimes called the ____ number.
e: The atomic number is sometimes called the proton number. Proton here means the positive particle inside the nucleus. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons.

q: The chemical properties of an element is determined by the number of electrons in the atom, that is atomic ____.
e: The chemical properties of an element is determined by the number of electrons in the atom, that is atomic number. The physics in this sentence is built around number.

q: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom is called the mass number (or) the ____ number.
e: The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom is called the mass number (or) the nucleon number. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: The mass number of an element is given the symbol ____.
e: The mass number of an element is given the symbol $A$. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: An atom of an element with atomic number $Z$ and the mass number $A$ is represented by its chemical symbol $X$ as ____.
e: An atom of an element with atomic number $Z$ and the mass number $A$ is represented by its chemical symbol $X$ as $_{Z}^{A}X$. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Mass number = Number of neutrons + Number of protons = Number of ____.
e: Mass number = Number of neutrons + Number of protons = Number of nucleons. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Number of neutrons = Mass number - Number of Proton = Mass number - Atomic ____.
e: Number of neutrons = Mass number - Number of Proton = Mass number - Atomic Number. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: Number of neutrons = ____.
e: Number of neutrons = $A - Z$. The physics in this sentence is built around $A - Z$.

q: Atoms that have the same atomic number but different neutron numbers (and thus different mass numbers) are called ____.
e: Atoms that have the same atomic number but different neutron numbers (and thus different mass numbers) are called isotopes. Z counts protons. A counts protons plus neutrons. Electrons orbit outside.

q: They have identical chemical properties, although their atoms have different ____.
e: They have identical chemical properties, although their atoms have different masses. The physics in this sentence is built around masses.

q: Most elements are a mixture of two (or) more ____.
e: Most elements are a mixture of two (or) more isotopes. The physics in this sentence is built around isotopes.

q: Hydrogen has three isotopes protium or hydrogen ($^1_1 H$), deuterium ($^2_1 H$) and ____ ($^3_1 H$).
e: Hydrogen has three isotopes protium or hydrogen ($^1_1 H$), deuterium ($^2_1 H$) and tritium ($^3_1 H$). The physics in this sentence is built around tritium.
